main_body: Two-storey half-timbered house: a large terracotta tile roof (rows 0-43) over a cream plaster front wall with timber frame, door, windows and a sign (rows 44-95).
top_band: Terracotta tile roof slope, rows 1-43 (L about 104-188, with per-tile highlights), ending in a lighter eave edge at about rows 40-43. The cream wall face starts at row 44.
evidence: The roof reads as a big foreshortened slope above the vertical wall, like the Beodeul house references. It is separated from the wall by a lighter eave edge and a darker band under it. The door has a dark frame and a lintel. The windows have shutters and sills, and the stone base is a separate band. There is no receding side face, so the 3/4 contract is met.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 tones and per-tile highlights, and the median of 15 colours per tile is close to the references (18 and 11). But 73% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% on the references, so the black sticker-like silhouette outline is clearly visible along the roof sides and the wall edges. The total of 47 distinct colours is well below the references (185 and 66). The plaster walls and the stone base are fairly flat, with 9% flat-fill coverage against 0% on both references, with only sparse speckle dots. It is clean but flatter and more sticker-like than the references.
